one_line: This is a skilled electrical generator and ATS job in Kuwait. It requires a valid Kuwait commercial license, at least two recent rentals of diesel generators rated 400 kVA or more, and local crews who can reach the site within 2 hours. Our documents show none of these.
scope: The U.S. Embassy Kuwait wants a contractor to rent, deliver, install, commission, operate, maintain, fuel, and finally remove two 500 kVA standby diesel generators (Caterpillar C15, Cummins, or equal). The work includes an 800 A Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS) for each unit, 5,000 L fuel tanks, and 240 sq mm cabling to the main isolator at U.S. Government residences at SDH. The base period is one month starting about December 20, 2026, with four one-month options. The order is firm-fixed-price in KWD and goes to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable, responsible quoter.
fit: The acquisition is unrestricted. SF-1449 Block 10 has no set-aside box checked, and the bid pack says 'Set-aside: none stated.' Our SBE/MBE status therefore doesn't block us.
NAICS 532490 is on our capability statement.
SAM is active (UEI REVFD44JLMV5, CAGE 57C31), so we only need to give our UEI and can skip FAR 52.204-90.
Our profile lists 'generators' under the Facility Support and Utilities core competency and claims worldwide project experience.
The profile lists a 24/7 emergency line, a dedicated service coordinator, and weekly QC reporting. These match the SOW's 24/7 hotline and monthly reporting in part.
red_flags: Section 3, Business Qualification, requires a valid Kuwait commercial registration or business license to rent, install, and maintain generators in Kuwait. DOSAR 652.242-73 also requires us to warrant authorization to do business in Kuwait. Our profile shows no Kuwait license or entity.

Past performance must include at least 2 contracts in the last 5 years for renting, installing, commissioning, or maintaining diesel generators of 400 kVA or more. Section 4 counts past performance as relevant only if it involves renting emergency diesel generators and ATS panels. None of our six references involves generators or ATS work.

Our PSC codes are W023, W099, and W045. This is PSC W061, and our price list has no generators, ATS, fuel, or cabling. We would be reselling a subcontractor's equipment and labor in an LPTA competition, which leaves little margin.

SOW 7.4 requires on-site arrival within 2 hours of a call, a repair within 8 hours, or a replacement unit within 24 hours. Section 3 also requires us to name our local service arrangements. Our stated standard is on-site response within 24 hours from US depots.

SOW 8.2 allows only qualified, licensed electricians to make connections, and the work must meet IEC 60364, ISO 8528, IEC 60947-6-1 or NFPA 70/110 and UL 1008, plus OBO requirements. Our documents name no licensed electrical personnel.

The site visit is in Kuwait on Nov 24, 2026 at 11:00 AM Kuwait time. Attendee names, Civil ID numbers, and nationalities are due by Nov 22, 2026 at 10:00 AM Kuwait time. That is 3 days from today, and Civil IDs imply Kuwait residents. Attendance is 'strongly encouraged' rather than mandatory, but FAR 52.237-1 puts any cost errors from skipping it on us.

We must buy Defense Base Act insurance from a DOL-approved carrier for covered employees (FAR 52.228-3, DOSAR 652.228-71). We must also price in KWD with no adjustment for currency or cost changes (Section 1, 2.3).
SOW 11.1 makes the contractor absolutely liable for injury and damage caused by our personnel's negligence, independent of insurance.

The diesel fuel supply needs a supplier with Kuwait commercial authorization and written confirmation of fuel availability (Section 3, Diesel Fuel Supply Capability). The prime remains fully responsible.

Crane work on Embassy property needs POSHO approval, a lift plan, and crane inspection and load-test certificates (Attachment 1). Under DOSAR 652.236-70, a Site Safety and Health Plan per EM 385-1-1 is due 10 working days before site work.
Section 4 refers to a 'Past Performance Confidence Rating table, below,' but no such table appears in the solicitation.
competition: No incumbent is named. The agency's only past award under NAICS 532490 was a $12,336 tent rental (PoP 2023) to 'Miscellaneous Foreign Awardees,' with 3 offers. Across agencies, the nearest generator benchmarks went to established generator rental firms: N C Power Systems, Sunbelt Rentals, Aggreko, and United Rentals. A 2017 'Lease of Generators and Floodlights' award to Omang Technologies & Trading drew 3 offers (place not listed). Most NAICS 532490 + PSC W061 awards drew 1 offer.
price_signal: HigherGov estimates this requirement at 35,000–85,000, currency not stated. The bid pack has no figures for comparable embassy generator awards. The closest comparables are N C Power Systems: $56,200 for a 750 kW diesel generator rental for 5 months (Bremerton, WA, Jan–Jun 2026) and $17,000 for a 1600 A ATS lease (2025–2026). Others are Sunbelt Rentals: $93,704 for a VA Honolulu rental generator over 12 months; Aggreko: $122,981 for about 1 month (East Orange, NJ); and Omang Technologies: $66,155 for generators and floodlights over about 7 weeks (2017). Our price list has no generator, ATS, or fuel rates, so we have no cost basis of our own.
must_have: Email the quote to Kuwait_Solicitation@state.gov with the subject 'Quote for RFQ: 19KU2027Q0005- Diesel Generator Rental with ATS' by Dec 8, 2026, 10:00 AM Kuwait time. Late quotes are not accepted (cover letter; SF-1449 Block 8).
Submit ten separate attachments with the exact file names given (Section 3, 52.212-1, Attachments and file format). Attachment 10 (Price) must be Microsoft Word.
Completed and signed SF-1449: Blocks 12, 17, 19–24, and 30a/b/c, plus signed copies of any amendments (Section 3 checklist; cover letter).
Completed Offeror Submission Checklist with page references for every item (Section 3, item 3).

Introduction: legal name, address, phone, and email; a valid Kuwait commercial license; UEI; a contact person; completed Section 5 reps and certs; and a 30-day offer validity (Section 3 checklist, Introduction).
Business Qualification: a valid Kuwait commercial registration or business license, and our plan to obtain all locally required licenses and permits (Section 3, Technical 1; SOW 12.0).

Past performance: at least 2 contracts in the last 5 years renting, installing, commissioning, or maintaining diesel generators of 400 kVA or more, each with customer, generator capacity, period, scope, and contact (Section 3, Technical 2).
Qualified technical personnel for installation, electrical connections, ATS configuration, commissioning, maintenance, and emergency repair, with certifications (Section 3, Technical 3).
Written confirmation that the generators and equipment are owned, leased, or available within the mobilization period (Section 3, Technical 4).
Maintenance and emergency support: local service arrangements and confirmation of the 2-hour, 8-hour, and 24-hour response times (Section 3; SOW 7.4).

Diesel fuel supply: supplier identity, the supplier's commercial authorization, written confirmation of fuel availability, a fuel-specification statement, and the monitoring plan (Section 3, Technical 5).
Installation and performance plan covering schedule, commissioning approach, preventive maintenance and emergency support, fuel replenishment, and decommissioning (Section 3, Technical 6).
For an 'equal' generator: manufacturer, brand, model, country of manufacture, data sheets, and proof it meets each salient characteristic (SOW 4.1).
Fuel tank sizing calculation for 72 hours at 100% load, based on manufacturer data (SOW 4.2.2).
Firm-fixed prices in KWD with no VAT for CLINs 0001–0008, the per-liter price for additional fuel, and the grand-total summary, including DBA costs (Section 1, 2.1–2.10).
DOSAR 652.228-70 DBA table of covered employee categories and counts (Section 2).
DOSAR 652.239-801: disclose any AI use in contract performance in the offer (Section 2).
Minimum insurance of US$10,000 bodily injury and US$30,000 property damage, plus workers' compensation per FAR 52.228-3 (SOW 11).
